newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The fall in the price of petrol and in revenues coming from customs tariffs are the two main reasons for the subsequent drop in state incoming revenues for the first three months of 1997. The discrepancy in target and real figures is due to wrong calculations in the increase of revenues for this year's budget.

--The second tender of Cretabank looks to receive a totally different response with the latest indicators on the bank's standing providing a good reason for bidders to come forward. The proclamation of the tender will be published on May 4.

--The first tax returns, due to be issued immediately after the Easter break, will prove to see an increase in declared incomes in the order of 20 percent and in taxation by 47 percent, due mainly to the non-indexation of the tax scale.

--National Capital is to put the Porto Carras resort complex - including the hotel, marina and golf courses, winery and trademarks - under the hammer on behlaf of three state-run banks which make up the bulk of the complex's creditors.
--The Bank of Greece's annual report on the Greek economy - presented last week - comes under the microscope by five professors of economics.
--The 650-billion drachma state procurements programme for 1997 will be released in mid-May and is hoped will bolster Greek industry. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
